newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SUMMER BREAK DISAPPEARS AS SWISS LOOK AHEAD TO NEW SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SUMMER BREAK DISAPPEARS AS SWISS LOOK AHEAD TO NEW SEASON.

text.p: European soccer fans who dread the summer break have nothing to fear this year, because there isn't going to be one.
For just seven days after Barcelona meet Real Betis in the Spanish Cup Final in Madrid to bring down the curtain on the 1996-97 season, the 1997-98 league season kicks off in Switzerland.

The Swiss league starts earlier than usual because of the national team's preparations for next year's World Cup finals in France. Switzerland play an all-important qualifier in Hungary on August 20. With the Spanish Cup Final taking place on June 28, and the Swiss League starting on July 5, the break between the seasons has been eroded -- and that is not accounting for the Intertoto Cup matches which are played throughout the summer.

The competition, now in its third season, got underway last weekend, and continues until the end of August by which time some of Europe's biggest clubs may already have been eliminated from the European Cup.
That competition kicks off on July 23 when the first legs of the preliminary round are scheduled to be played.
While there has been reports recently that FIFA want to introduce a new competition for continental champions clubs, introducing European soccer all-year round, the truth is, it has already arrived.
"There are still breaks, but they are less noticeable because action is still going on in other places," FIFA spokesman Andreas Herren said on Tuesday.
In effect there will hardly be any break from competitive soccer in Europe for at least another two years -- although there could be a brief respite for a few weeks from the middle of July next year.
The World Cup is due to start in France on June 10 and end on July 12 1998 -- with the chances high that some league or cup competitions will already be underway by the end of that month.
